mem.10:
Deborah and Jolene — memory through 22 March 2023

**January 2023**
- Jolene completed a demanding electrical-engineering project during 16–22 January. She read Neal Stephenson’s *Avalanche* in one sitting around 21 January.
- Deborah visits her late mother’s former home; sitting by her mother’s favorite window seat brings peace and a sense of her presence. Her mother loved reading there every night, travel, and the morning view. Deborah shared a photo of sky from an airplane. Her mother died a few years ago; Jolene’s mother died in 2022.
- Both wear pendants honoring their mothers. Jolene’s heart-shaped bird pendant was a gift from her mother in Paris in 2010, symbolizing freedom and pursuing goals. Deborah shared a photo of herself and her mother hugging in wheelchairs; Jolene shared a bench by her mother’s window.
- Deborah’s father died suddenly on 25 January. Her family was shocked; spending time together and looking at photos brought comfort. Her parents married in 1993. Deborah and her husband hope to build a loving, open, mutually supportive family. On 26 January her group sent a thank-you letter praising her positive influence.
- Yoga helped Deborah through a difficult time and inspired her to teach and share peace and joy.
- Jolene’s snakes are Susie and Seraphim; they calm her and make her happy. Seraphim once escaped while she gamed, then curled up beside her. Jolene shared a photo of Seraphim peeking from a blanket. She said she bought “it” in Paris a year earlier (unclear referent).
- Jolene and her partner enjoy console games, including *Detroit*. She learned gaming on her own as a child. They planned to play *Walking Dead* on 4 February. A photo showed someone in bed with a dog watching TV.

**February–March 2023**
- 31 January Deborah met neighbor Anna at park yoga; they discussed yoga’s personal and community benefits. On 3 February they tried dance poses, including Warrior II, and exchanged chair-yoga tips. Deborah shared a studio photo of them posing.
- Jolene built a sustainable water purifier for a rural community as a robotics project for her engineering professor. On 4 February, seeing it work felt purposeful; she wants to create sustainable solutions for disadvantaged communities.
- Jolene liked *Sapiens* for its history and technology and was inspired by stories of overcoming challenges. Deborah shared a friend’s bouquet, which gave her hope. Deborah likes a park’s forest trail near a beach. Jolene shared a Bogotá beach/surfboard photo from summer 2022; sunsets over water feel calming.
- Deborah finds peace on a small island near her mother’s old home and brings her mother’s amulet; holding it makes her feel her mother’s love. Anna also wears a memorial pendant.
- On 8 February Jolene took a “dope” mini-retreat to assess her life. It gave her confidence and a new outlook; she made more progress than expected, developed engineering solutions, and felt excited about her project. She wanted to explore green technology for disadvantaged areas.
- Jolene proposed a volunteer STEM program for underprivileged children through schools or community centers, with workshops and guest speakers. She had not contacted organizations and wanted to refine the idea; she shared planner sketches/notes.
- On 21 February Jolene had dinner/drinks with friends and shared a food-and-wine photo. Deborah visited a nostalgic, calming garden with flowers in buckets; roses and dahlias bring her peace. She went for comfort after a friend died the prior week. Karlie was the deceased friend; Deborah’s shared photo was the last of them together, taken hiking the previous summer, and makes her smile. Image description: two women on a motorcycle on a dirt road.
- Deborah’s favorite trip was Bali in 2022: peaceful, beautiful, good for yoga; she shared a beach swing photo. Jolene wanted to try beach yoga and report back.
- On 25 February Jolene said she balances engineering school and her partner’s video games with yoga and meditation, which help her relax, gain perspective, and manage stress. Her partner sometimes joins; yoga relaxes them and brings them closer. Together three years, unmarried and taking things slowly; met in a college engineering class, became friends then partners. They enjoy engineering together and understand each other’s struggles. A photo showed their hands with rings; his was decorative, not a wedding ring. Other photos showed a book/calculator and men outside a building.
- Deborah’s self-care routine: morning meditation, yoga, teaching, and evenings with loved ones. She began jogging at a nearby park on 24 February; exercise connects her to her body. Her saying: “can’t pour from an empty cup.” She shared a sunset photo of someone on a bench as a reminder to find peace amid chaos.
- On 2 March Anna brought Deborah vegan tofu-and-vegetable stir-fry with ginger and soy sauce. Jolene’s favorite comfort food is lasagna; she was busy with studies/exams. Jolene wants to monitor stress and mental health; she sometimes gets caught up in studies and forgets self-care. Deborah said yoga resets her mind. Jolene shared photos of a wood-floor room with a window, and a purse/plant on a table. Deborah offered her a mug like a pictured yellow cup with a handwritten message; Jolene said it cheered her up.
- The previous Sunday Jolene took Seraphim to the park; it explored among leaves, and people are surprised to see a tamed snake outdoors. Jolene shared a snake/lizard-like animal photo.
- Jolene finds studies, exams, and deadlines overwhelming and wanted to be more mindful. She shared a desk photo with notebook and computer to-do list. Deborah suggested breaking work into smaller tasks, setting goals, using a planner, and protecting self-care time; offered help making a study plan. Deborah enjoys birdsong and a gentle breeze outdoors.
- On 13 March Deborah had started a neighborhood yoga class after neighbors showed interest; first class was Friday. Teaching felt calming, spread awareness, made her happy, and helped build friendships/community. She shared a group photo of women. Jolene praised sharing something one loves and supporting others. Jolene struggled with engineering assignments and wanted to discuss time management; Deborah agreed to find a suitable time. Jolene would check her schedule; Deborah offered support and encouraged self-care.

**22 March 2023**
- Jolene said keeping up with exams/deadlines and finding time for everything was stressful. She uses Pomodoro (25 minutes work, 5-minute break) but struggles to prioritize. Deborah shared a photo of her daily to-do list; Jolene shared a photo of her notes from the previous Friday and said a large task list overwhelms her. Deborah explained the Eisenhower Matrix (importance/urgency), sharing a photo of scissors on paper. Jolene found the visualization helpful and agreed to try it.
- Deborah shared a beach photo of someone walking with a surfboard, saying she and Anna had watched a sunset by the sea and realized they inspire each other. Jolene said it made her think of learning to surf. She had gathered information, watched videos, and bought a beginner’s guide, but needed time/place for a lesson. Deborah encouraged her; a photo of surfboards leaning against a palm tree motivated Jolene. Deborah urged her to enjoy each step, not just the result; Jolene thanked her.
mem.20:
Deborah and Jolene — memory through 21 August 2023

**January 2023**

Her mother loved travel and art. Jolene’s heart-shaped bird pendant was a 2010 Paris gift from her mother, representing freedom and pursuing goals; her mother died in 2022. Both shared photos with their mothers and wear pendants honoring them.
- Around 21 Jan, Jolene finished a demanding electrical-engineering project and read Neal Stephenson’s *Avalanche* in one sitting.

- Jolene’s snakes are Susie and Seraphim. Caring for them calms her. Seraphim once escaped while she gamed and curled up beside her. Jolene and her partner enjoy console games, including *Detroit* and *The Walking Dead*.

**February–March**
- Deborah met neighbor Anna at park yoga on 31 Jan; they practiced poses and exchanged chair-yoga tips on 3 Feb. By 13 Mar Deborah had started a neighborhood yoga class, enjoying sharing exercise and its positive effects.
- Jolene built a sustainable water purifier for a rural community as an engineering-professor robotics project; seeing it work on 4 Feb felt purposeful. She likes *Sapiens*, hopes to develop sustainable solutions/green tech, and proposed a volunteer STEM program for underprivileged children (not yet developed or acted on). A mini-retreat helped her find engineering solutions and confidence; she described an emotional rollercoaster.
- Deborah likes a forest trail near a beach and an island near her mother’s former home. Jolene shared a Bogotá beach/surfboard photo from summer 2022; waterside sunsets calm her. In February she researched surfing, watched videos and bought a beginner’s guide, but had not found a lesson. Deborah’s favorite trip was peaceful Bali in 2022, where she did yoga.
- Jolene and her partner had been together three years, unmarried and taking things slowly. They met as college engineering friends, share engineering/gaming interests, and do yoga together. A hand photo showed his decorative, not wedding, ring. He helps her focus when gaming is tough; they like cooperative *It Takes Two*.
- Deborah’s self-care includes morning meditation, yoga, teaching, loved ones and jogging; on 24 Feb she jogged in a nearby park and planned to make it daily. Motto: “can’t pour from an empty cup.” Jolene also uses yoga/meditation, but can neglect self-care during study.
- Anna brought vegan tofu-vegetable stir-fry with ginger/soy on 2 Mar; Jolene’s comfort food is lasagna. March exams/deadlines stressed Jolene. She uses Pomodoro (25 min work/5 break); Deborah advised task breakdown, planning and self-care, and introduced the Eisenhower Matrix, which Jolene planned to try.
- Jolene took Seraphim to a park to explore leaves; people are surprised by a tame snake. She reported an engineering breakthrough on 28 Mar. Deborah bought yoga props and a candle. Jolene likes lavender/rosemary, Nils Frahm and Ólafur Arnalds; Deborah likes candles/essential oils, mellow instrumentals, “Savana,” and recommended *Sleep* for meditation.

**April–June**
- Deborah biked with a neighbor and visited an art show with a friend on 9 Apr. Art reminds her of her mother; she feels they experience it together, both painfully and comfortingly.
- Jolene completed a difficult, exciting solar-powered vehicle project in May, with a solar panel on its back; by 6 Jun she was proud she persisted. In June she interned at a well-known engineering firm. The intense work gave real-world experience but strained work/life balance and left little time for hobbies; she shared a photo of construction-worker colleagues.
- On 24 Jun Jolene bought a plant-filled aquarium enclosure for Seraphim (gotten in 2022).
- On 26 Jun Deborah prepared for a yoga retreat with friends for connection, peace and understanding; shared group park-yoga and beach Dancer Pose photos. Jolene felt overwhelmed by internship but rewarded by a breakthrough and wanted a retreat. Deborah said her retreat helped her reflect and feel centered; shared a lake sunset/boat photo. Other photos: a house drawing with rulers (unclear context) and three people doing tree pose before a large peace/enlightenment statue.

**July–August**
- By 9 Jul Deborah had started a running group with Anna; Jolene fit workouts around study. Photos included three men on a road and a woman with skateboard (unclear context).
- Deborah runs and practices yoga/meditation with others and organizes mindfulness/self-care events for well-being and community.
- Jolene got snakes from fascination with reptiles. Susie was adopted in 2021 when Jolene felt lonely and reminds her to stay strong and find joy in small things. After a snake escaped and she searched for hours, she found it snuggled under her bed, feeling love and gratitude. Snake photos showed one on a branch/book and one in a sand-and-plant tank. Jolene finds snake care and nature calming.
- Deborah dislikes dogs, has two cats (photo of them under a blanket on a couch), and said she takes them for park runs morning/evening. Jolene joked snakes don’t run and wanted more walks. Both find nature restorative; Jolene enjoys walks and photos and shared a waterside sunset and hidden-gem lake dock, suggesting Deborah visit.
- On 1 Aug Deborah started a community cleanup project and was fundraising; pleased people were coming together. Jolene’s project crashed the prior week and she lost all files, feeling frustrated and depressed. Pets and games helped; yoga and meditation restored calm. Deborah shared routine ideas and said her favorite yoga is gentle, breath- and grounding-focused flow.
- By 12 Aug Deborah had made a meditation guide for her retreat. Meditation helped Jolene regain clarity amid stress over lost work. Jolene shared two blue-covered, white-striped notebooks decorated with space/engines, galaxies and circuitry; art/design gives her a different perspective on problems. She was developing a prototype for more productive, affordable aerial surveillance for emergency response and environmental monitoring, aiming to make the world safer.
- On 16 Aug Jolene said plans felt up and down after checking in with her boyfriend; balancing engineering, relationship and personal growth was hard. A checklist-book photo accompanied this. Deborah encouraged balance/self-care and shared a room with moss wall and floor cushion. Jolene started a bullet journal; checking off tasks felt satisfying.

**21 August 2023**
- Jolene said she and her partner had received *Battlefield 1* for their console the previous week.
- Deborah revisited a memory-filled place and sat on a bench where she used to chat; she felt nostalgia, longing and gratitude. She brought flowers because her mother loved them and appreciated life’s simple things; a photo showed a flower cart, flowers placed on a street, and a woman holding red roses. Her mother taught her to slow down, notice beauty and find joy.
- They agreed busy life can obscure small pleasures. Jolene was trying to do more yoga and meditation for relaxation/focus. Deborah’s grounding habits are yoga, meditation, mindful walks; a waterside sunset photo. She calls walks a “reboot.”
- Jolene shared a green cushion by a window and said her favorite resting yoga pose is savasana/corpse pose: calming, helps her let go and surrender. A humorous photo showed a person lying on the floor with a paper bag. She had practiced yoga for three years, as an escape from study/work stress, and said she was finding her zen again.
mem.30:
Deborah & Jolene — memory through 20 September 2023

**Family, pets, grief**
- Deborah’s mother (loved art, travel, flowers and simple beauty) died before these conversations; her father died suddenly on 25 January 2023. Her parents married in 1993. Her mother was a devoted cook who baked her pineapple birthday cakes, making her feel special and bringing family together. Deborah finds comfort in photos, yoga and visiting meaningful places; art can both hurt and comfort. On 10 September she sat at her mother’s former home and felt her loving presence. On 15 September she reconnected with her mother’s friends and shared memories/photos, including a pajama mirror selfie with her mother.
- Jolene’s mother died in 2022. A heart-shaped bird pendant her mother gave her in Paris in 2010 symbolizes freedom and pursuing goals. Her mother taught perseverance (“never give up”) and helping others. Deborah and Jolene share memories and photos of their mothers and meaningful pendants.
- Deborah’s cats: Max (her late mother’s cat; turned 8 on 26 August 2023) and Luna (adopted, age 5). Photo: Luna on left, both by a windowsill.
- Jolene’s snakes: Susie (with her since 2021; comfort, strength and enjoying small things) and Seraphim (since 2022; planted aquarium enclosure added June 2023). Snake care calms her. One female escaped and was found under a bed; Jolene took Seraphim to a park to explore leaves. On 15 September she shared a photo holding Susie, her two-year companion.
- Jolene and her male partner have been together about three years as of 2023. They met as engineering-college friends, play games and do yoga, are unmarried and take things slowly. His late father encouraged determination; her partner pursues creative work.

**Deborah**
- Yoga teacher, including neighborhood classes. Met neighbor Anna at park yoga 31 January, exchanged chair-yoga tips 3 February, hosted class 10 March, began neighborhood classes by 13 March. Chair twist: sit at edge, feet planted, twist with hand on knee, hold breaths, switch. Yoga supports balance and reconnection. Enjoys beach yoga, nature, meditation, candles/oils and mellow music (“Savana,” Sleep). Meditation was indispensable by 6 September. Self-care includes meditation, teaching, jogging, mindful walks and loved ones; motto: “can’t pour from an empty cup.” Encourages Jolene to breathe, break work into tasks, stretch/walk, sleep and balance self-care.
- Favorite trip Bali (2022); loves forest trails, beaches, nature and an island near her mother’s former home. Yoga retreat near her mother’s place in August 2023 was life-changing. Brought flowers to a meaningful bench 21 August; shared a favorite lake-reflection spot 30 August. Yoga friends feel like family; her mother was her biggest fan and attended classes. Led meditation-yoga for care-home seniors the week of 7 August.
- Organized a yoga event with food stalls/live music in July. On 16 September she and a neighbor ran a free community gardening class for all ages; she loved sharing plants and helping people care for the world.
- A group thanked her for her positive influence in a letter on 26 January. A deceased friend wrote “Let go of what no longer serves you”; Deborah misses her and said she could not support her.
- Beach is special: she married there and discovered surfing; ocean, sand and fresh air bring peace. On 17 September invited Jolene to surf; they tentatively planned for October, pending schedules. Deborah has surfed; Jolene had just begun learning but had not yet surfed.

**Jolene**
- Engineering student/professor, interested in sustainable technology and social impact: rural water-purifier prototype (4 February), solar vehicle project finished May, engineering-firm internship June. Aerial-surveillance project for emergencies/environment crashed in late July and files were lost; she kept persevering. Wants affordable emergency/environmental monitoring, renewables, clean water, environmental solutions, STEM volunteering for disadvantaged kids and engineering for communities.
- Likes *Sapiens*. Presented at a virtual conference shortly before 24 August and got positive feedback. Decorates blue/white-striped notebooks with space, engines, galaxies and circuitry. Uses Pomodoro (25/5), task breakdown and the Eisenhower Matrix (Deborah’s idea); lists can overwhelm. Started a bullet journal in August to schedule study, classes and personal time. Balancing relationship, engineering and growth is difficult; yoga/meditation sometimes neglected. Practiced yoga about three years and likes savasana. Deborah offered study-planning help, but no meeting was set.
- Likes Nils Frahm, Ólafur Arnalds, lavender/rosemary, lasagna, walks, photography, sunsets and water. Read Neal Stephenson’s *Avalanche* in one sitting in January. Bought a beginner surfing guide in February.
- Gaming relaxes her; her mother played games with her, and she got a Nintendo at 10. *Monster Hunter: World* is a favorite with memories of her mother. Likes immersive stories/open worlds; planned *The Walking Dead* with partner in January, had a mini-retreat 1 February, bought him an Xbox in August. Shared Wii photo 3 September and Xbox/Yoda photo 17 August.
- Nearby tranquil pond is her meditation place. Jolene and partner returned from an “awesome” Rio trip on 29 August (yoga, cafes, old temple; shared mirror-yoga and temple-stairs photos). Planned camping for nature/yoga on 8 September. On 12 September said they had gone the previous weekend to a meditation retreat in Phuket for a few weeks; loved nature/reflection and learned to make room for relaxation alongside study. A session on releasing expectations/judgments and savoring the present stood out. On 15 September said she and partner tried scuba diving on 8 September, loved it, found a dive spot and she may pursue certification.

**Recent conversations**
- **17 September:** Deborah shared food, pineapple cake (smiley face) and mixer/whisk photos while discussing her mother’s cooking. Jolene shared chocolate-chip cookies; likes warm gooey chocolate and soft buttery cookies. They discussed reading: Jolene said a self-discovery book resonated with her and shared her aesthetically styled bathroom; Deborah shared her living-room bookshelf/couch. Deborah showed beach/surf photos and confirmed she had surfed; they tentatively planned a surf outing in October, with Jolene to check her schedule.
- **20 September:** Deborah enjoyed dancing at a music festival with friends; music brings people together and reminded her of her mother singing lullabies. Jolene shared a photo of herself and her partner at a festival the prior year, and said festivals help her express herself and escape daily stress. She had just returned from a yoga-retreat trip with her partner; sunrise over a valley was colorful and beautiful, making her feel alive, grateful, peaceful and connected to nature and herself. She recalled a peaceful waterfall oasis found on a hike with her partner, where her worries disappeared, and plans another nature outing next month. Deborah shared a pink blossom tree near her home, which bloomed magically each spring and inspired awe, appreciation of life and hope for growth. Jolene shared a plant growing out of a building corner as a symbol of resilience; both valued noticing small positives and growing through tough times.
